verdict.why: X gives the implementer a usable first release without waiting on either external service. Its Rollout specifies one backlog row, a dated board reply (2026-12-07 for persona configurations; 2026-12-21 conditional on stand readiness), and manual panel updates until the super-ux template lands. Both options preserve the scenario × persona budget and leave agent-tester unchanged. X is stronger on evidence: C4 resolves a comparison persona to the same step, pass and round; C6–C7 and T-15–T-19 check the reused capture's cell, step, bytes and, when supplied, build ID without putting the gate on the network. Y has useful safeguards worth retaining: R9 forbids an ‘only here’ claim on a row with an unrealised axis, and R18 preserves resource accounting for stand reads. But Y explicitly allows a nonexistent comparison row to escape detection (Edge cases), and its C5 example makes the very claim R9 forbids. Its Rollout also substitutes ‘next minor’ for the requested date, creates a backlog row even for no change, and ties panel adoption to another project's release.
risks: X's phase-two date is conditional, not a confirmed stand capability. Q5–Q6 leave the export contract and sender key unresolved; Stand intake step 4 excludes untagged explore screenshots, so those runs save no capture work.

X C7/T-19 lets a stand row pass without --build, leaving stale evidence possible despite the agent instruction to supply it. X C3's example also shows a complete config_applied alongside a config_gap that its own validator rejects.

Both options let wholly unconfigured panels keep passing. That avoids a disruptive migration but does not deliver the requested coverage until projects actually assign configurations to all ten portraits.
